'''Nazira Karodia''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|MBE|CChem|FRSC}} is a chemist, Professor of Science Education and Deputy Vice Chancellor at [[Edinburgh Napier University]] (2021&ndash;). She was previously Pro-Vice Chancellor for Regional Engagement at the [[University of Wolverhampton]]. She works on [[organic synthesis]], [[green chemistry]], [[heterocyclic compound]]s and science education.<ref name=wolves/>

== Early life and education ==
Karodia was born and grew up in [[South Africa]] under apartheid.<ref name=":0">{{cite journal|last1=Pain|first1=Elisabeth|title=Battling inequality for herself and others|journal=Science|year=2017|issn=0036-8075|doi=10.1126/science.caredit.a1700018}}</ref> Like most people not of European origin, she suffered from racial segregation during her schooling. She was able to study chemistry at the [[University of Natal]], which had been only for white people, and she graduated in 1990.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/topics-policy/diversity-in-science/parent-carer-scientist/nazira-karodia/|title=Professor Nazira Karodia |publisher=[[Royal Society]]|website=royalsociety.org|language=en-GB|access-date=2018-09-06}}</ref> She left South Africa in 1992.<ref name=":1" /> Karodia completed her [[PhD]] at the [[University of St Andrews]],<ref name=nkphd>{{cite thesis|oclc=1049717145|degree=PhD|publisher=University of St Andrews|hdl=10023/15005|title=Preparation, structure and reactivity of some new types of stabilised phosphorus ylides|first= Nazira|last=Karodia|date=1996|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.750669}}}} {{free access}}</ref> working on phosphorus [[ylide]] supervised by Alan Aitken in 1995.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Aitken|first1=R. == Career and research==
Karodia joined the [[University of Florida]] as a fellow in the Centre for Heterocyclic Chemistry where she worked on developed [[Benzothiazine]]s and [[Benzotriazole]]s.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Katritzky|first1=Alan R.|last2=Wang|first2=Jin|last3=Karodia|first3=Nazira|last4=Li|first4=Jianqing|date=1997|title=A Novel Transformation of Esters to Alkynes with 1-Substituted Benzotriazoles|journal=The Journal of Organic Chemistry|language=en|volume=62|issue=12|pages=4142–4147|doi=10.1021/jo962291t|issn=0022-3263}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|date=1997|title=Facile Synthesis of Benzotriazines and Indoles by Ring-Scissions of α-Benzotriazol-1-yl Hydrazones|journal=Synthetic Communications|language=en|volume=27|issue=22|pages=3963–3976|doi=10.1080/00397919708005918|issn=0039-7911}}</ref> Karodia was appointed senior lecturer at the [[University of Bradford]] and made director for STEM in 1998.<ref name=":1" /> Here Karodia developed her interest in science education and science outreach programs that looked to benefit the local community. She was a senior member of the [[Higher Education Funding Council for England]] (HEFCE) STEM programme, where she was made Regional Director (Yorkshire, Humber and North East) of the National HE STEM programme.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hestem.ac.uk/node/958|title=National HE STEM Programme - University of Birmingham|website=www.hestem.ac.uk|language=en-gb|access-date=2018-09-06}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite news|url=https://www.educationopportunities.co.uk/dr-nazira-karodia/|title=Dr Nazira Karodia - NEON|work=NEON|access-date=2018-09-06|language=en-GB}}</ref> Her chemistry research focused on ionic liquids and liquid crystalline polymers.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=El Mansoury|first1=Ahmed|last2=Bushby|first2=Richard J.|last3=Karodia|first3=Nazira|date=2012|title=Triphenylene-based discotic liquid crystals: star-shaped oligomers and branched-chain polymers|journal=Liquid Crystals|language=en|volume=39|issue=10|pages=1222–1230|doi=10.1080/02678292.2012.707691|s2cid=96351481|issn=0267-8292}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|date=2006-11-27|title=The ionic liquid ethyltri-n-butylphosphonium tosylate as solvent for the acid-catalysed hetero-Michael reaction|journal=Tetrahedron|language=en|volume=62|issue=48|pages=11039–11043|doi=10.1016/j.tet.2006.09.052|issn=0040-4020|last1=Karodia|first1=Nazira|last2=Liu|first2=Xihan|last3=Ludley|first3=Petra|last4=Pletsas|first4=Dimitrios|last5=Stevenson|first5=Grace|hdl=10454/3694}}</ref> Karodia is part of the European Union funded GENOVATE project: ''Transforming organisational culture for gender equality in research and innovation''.<ref name=wolves>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wlv.ac.uk/about-us/our-staff/nazira-karodia/|title=Nazira Karodia - University of Wolverhampton|website=www.wlv.ac.uk|language=en|access-date=2018-09-06|archive-date=4 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190704035530/https://www.wlv.ac.uk/about-us/our-staff/nazira-karodia/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.genovate.eu/dissemination/genovate-international-conference/speakers/nazira-karodia/|title=Nazira Karodia|website=www.genovate.eu|language=en|access-date=2018-09-06}}</ref>  She is also working on programmes to promote careers in science and engineering, especially for students from underrepresented parts of the community.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.raeng.org.uk/publications/other/student-ambassador-training|title=Disseminating student ambassador top-up training in engineering in Yorkshire and the Northeast region|last=Karodia|first=Nazira|access-date=2018-09-06|archive-date=21 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170721105111/http://www.raeng.org.uk/publications/other/student-ambassador-training|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Since 2021 she has held the position of Deputy Vice Chancellor at Edinburgh Napier University. Prior to this she worked at the [[University of Wolverhampton]] where she was Pro Vice Chancellor Regional Engagement (February 2020 – July 2021), Dean of the Faculty of Science and Engineering (February 2016 &ndash; January 2020) and Professor of Science Education.<ref>{{Citation|last=University of Wolverhampton|title=Research - Open Your Mind Campaign - Professor Nazira Karodia|date=2018-03-16|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m-JklpgN-xA|access-date=2018-09-06}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://leadinglearning.co.uk/professor-nazira-karodia/|title=Professor Nazira Karodia - Leading Learning|work=Leading Learning|access-date=2018-09-06|language=en-GB|archive-date=7 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180907032519/http://leadinglearning.co.uk/professor-nazira-karodia/|url-status=dead}}</ref>  She has partnered with the [[Doaba]] Group of Colleges.<ref name="Midlands Enterprise Universities">{{Cite news|url=http://midlandsenterpriseuniversities.co.uk/new-partnership-healthcare-course-launched|title=New partnership healthcare course launched - Midlands Enterprise Universities|date=2018-04-27|work=Midlands Enterprise Universities|access-date=2018-09-06|language=en-GB|archive-date=7 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180907032411/http://midlandsenterpriseuniversities.co.uk/new-partnership-healthcare-course-launched|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2018 she launched a new partnerships health science course.<ref name="Midlands Enterprise Universities"/>

==Awards and honours==
Karodia received a commendation from the National Educational Opportunities Network (NEON) in 2015 for Outstanding Contribution to Widening Access.<ref name=":2" /> She was selected as one of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]'s Top 175 Faces of Chemistry in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rsc.org/diversity/175-faces/all-faces/dr-nazira-karodia-cchem-frsc/|title=Dr Nazira Karodia CChem FRSC {{!}} 175 Faces of Chemistry|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200806021426/http://www.rsc.org/diversity/175-faces/all-faces/dr-nazira-karodia-cchem-frsc/|archivedate=6 August 2020|website=www.rsc.org|language=en|access-date=2018-09-06}}</ref> In 2017 she was honoured at the [[ShruthiUK]] [[Birmingham Thyagaraja Festival]] with a ''Women-in-Science award''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wlv.ac.uk/about-us/news-and-events/latest-news/2017/april-2017/dean-honoured-for-achievements-in-the-field-of-science.php|title=April 2017 - Dean honoured for achievements in the field of science - University of Wolverhampton|website=www.wlv.ac.uk|language=en|access-date=2018-09-06}}</ref> In 2015 she was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry]] (FRSC).<ref name=":1" />

Karodia was appointed [[Member of the Order of the British Empire]] (MBE) in the [[2022 New Year Honours]] for services to the chemical sciences.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=63571|supp=y|page=N21|date=1 January 2022}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Karodia has twin daughters, both of whom studied physics at university.<ref name=":0" /> She lost one twin to [[sickle cell disease]] in 2012.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.nouse.co.uk/2012/06/19/memorial-service-held-in-physics-for-%E2%80%9Csorely-missed%E2%80%9D-james-student/|title=Memorial service held in Physics for "sorely missed" James student|last=Banning-Lover|first=Rachel|date=2012-06-19|work=Nouse|access-date=2018-09-06|language=en-US}}</ref> The [[University of York]], where she was a student, have an award in her honour.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.york.ac.uk/physics/undergraduate/ug-academic-awards/|title=UG Academic Awards - Physics, The University of York|website=www.york.ac.uk|language=EN|access-date=2018-09-06}}</ref>
